newsitem.title: CANADA: CBRS reaffirms Alberta ratings with stable outlook.
newsitem.headline: CBRS reaffirms Alberta ratings with stable outlook.

text.p: Canadian Bond Rating Service on Wednesday said it reaffirmed Alberta's long- and short-term debt ratings at AA+ and A-1+ respectively with stable outlooks.

In confirming the ratings, the bond rating agency noted that the oil-rich economy grew by a healthy 3.2 percent in 1996, fueled by its interest-sensitive and export sectors, as well as stronger consumer spending. The agency said economic growth of 3.6 percent in 1997 and 4.1 percent in 1998 was expected for the province.

CBRS also noted that the province forecast a C$2.3 billion surplus for fiscal 1996-97 and planned to eliminate its C$3.9 billion net debt by fiscal 2005-2006. The net debt is the province's liabilities less the assets of its Heritage Fund.
The agency said when the net debt was paid down, the province would continue to pay interest on about C$9.5 billion of debt after fiscal 2005-2006.
